description: We're Zero Shot—a curious team passionate about tech, AI, and earth science. For the Field Shift challenge, we want to help farmers make smarter crop decisions using NASA climate and soil data. Our goal is simple: turn complex satellite data into easy, practical rotation plans that protect the soil and save water. Excited to collaborate, learn, and build something meaningful together!
summary: GREEN FUTURE is an AI-powered Agri-Spatial Decision-Support System developed by Team ZERO SHOT to help farmers design climate-resilient, water-saving crop rotations. By harmonizing 10 years of NASA and global Earth Observation data (SMAP, POWER, GPM, ERA5-Land, MODIS, and SoilGrids from 2016–2025) across 14 Egyptian governorates with a verified 51-crop agronomic database, our platform translates complex satellite telemetry into actionable seasonal plans. Using machine learning (R² = 87%) with explicit uncertainty bounds (± m³/m³) and an explainable Multi-Criteria Decision Engine (MCDA), it benchmarks three tailored rotations against traditional practices to cut irrigation water demand, restore soil fertility via natural nitrogen fixation, and break pest cycles. Built with a bilingual farmer-centered interface, interactive satellite maps, and an AI advisor (Eng. Rayan), GREEN FUTURE empowers sustainable agriculture while reinforcing the vital role of local extension engineers.
details:
What Does GREEN FUTURE Do & How Does It Work?

GREEN FUTURE is an end-to-end Agri-Spatial Decision-Support System (DSS) that transforms 10 years of NASA and global Earth Observation data (2016–2025) into personalized, climate-resilient crop rotation prescriptions for farmers.

Through an intuitive 3-step bilingual wizard (Arabic & English), a farmer or agricultural engineer enters their governorate (covering 14 major agricultural regions across Egypt), farm area in feddans, previous crop, irrigation availability, mechanization level, and market goals, alongside an interactive 90-day weather scenario simulator (Δ Temperature & Δ Rainfall). Behind the scenes, our system executes a 4-stage pipeline:

1. Multi-Sensor Data Fusion: Harmonizes 6 satellite and reanalysis missions (NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM, ERA5-Land, MODIS/GEDI, and SRTM/SoilGrids) onto a unified 10-day Dekadal grid (5,110 clean records × 18 core features).

2. AI Soil Moisture & Heat Forecasting: Uses a temporally validated Gradient Boosting / Random Forest ensemble (trained on 2016–2023, tested out-of-sample on 2024–2025, achieving R² = 87% and MAE = 0.014 m³/m³) paired with Quantile Regression uncertainty intervals (± m³/m³).

3. Explainable MCDA Rotation Engine: Evaluates 51 verified Egyptian crops to synthesize 3 tailored multi-season rotations and benchmarks them against the traditional baseline rotation (Wheat → Rice → Wheat) across water savings (ETc in m³), natural nitrogen fixation (urea bags saved), pest-cycle breaking (botanical family rotation), and salinity/heat tolerance.

4. Geospatial Lab & Eng. Rayan AI: Provides an interactive Esri satellite map with toggleable moisture, heat, and salinity layers, historical vs. forecast charts, a printable A4 multi-plan PDF prescription, and an embedded AI agronomic advisor (Eng. Rayan).

Benefits & Intended Impact

• Water Conservation: Reduces seasonal irrigation water demand by up to 35–49% (saving tens of thousands of cubic meters per farm) by matching low-ETc, drought-resilient crops to forecast soil moisture deficits.

• Soil Health & Input Reduction: Replaces synthetic nitrogen fertilizers through strategic legume integration (Faba Bean, Berseem Clover, Cowpea) and prevents soil erosion during bare fallow transitions.

• Farmer Empowerment & Transparency: Translates complex satellite telemetry into plain, actionable guidance while explicitly displaying prediction uncertainty and reminding users that remote sensing supports—never replaces—local soil lab tests (ECe) and agricultural extension engineers.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

• Data Engineering & Machine Learning: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn, LightGBM, Gradient Boosting, Quantile Regression, and Jupyter Notebooks.

• Web Platform & Geospatial Visualization: HTML5, CSS3 (Responsive Dark/Light UI), Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Leaflet.js (Esri World Imagery & OpenStreetMap), and Chart.js.

• AI Assistant & Deployment: Context-aware LLM integration (Eng. Rayan AI) and GitHub Pages CI/CD hosting.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Instead of offering a single generic crop recommendation, Team ZERO SHOT designed a comparative 4-strategy decision framework that accounts for real-world field constraints: canal water intermittency, well salinity, labor/machinery capacity, botanical pest cycles, and seasonal weather shocks—bridging space-borne Earth science with practical farm economics.
